declared_base_replacements.base_text: ## FVLT — v3.2.5 (on the v3.2.0 Semantic-Correction Baseline)

**Version:** 3.2.5 (current, **LOCKED release of record**, Robin 2026-07-14 "it is a lock"). This release assembles four locked kernel items at their declared seats plus two locked bibliography-tier entries; the assembled-release cold pass PASSED (Codex 2026-07-14, PASS-WITH-PATCHES, all folded). **v3.2.5 supersedes v3.2.4 as the locked release of record.** FVLT accretes as point-releases on the **v3.2.0 semantic-correction baseline**: the filename and this baseline heading name the *baseline*; the *current* point-version is stated here and in the bibliography changelog head; per-item `v3.x.y` tags record when each item entered. The v3.2.0 baseline preserves the source archive filename `fvlt_v3.24.skill` (internal version v3.1.24) provenance package while correcting theorem scope, notation, register separation, and release identity under the supplied audit; v3.2.1–v3.2.2 add the ℚ⁺ exponent-completion material (Rmk II.5c, OP 31), v3.2.3 adds the two-collapse-registers cluster (Cor II.23.2.2, Rmk II.23.2c); v3.2.4 adds the Goldbach-conjugation cluster (Rmk II.23.5a/b, Rmk VI.3a) with the Rmk 13.x → II.22a register-discipline reseat, the residence-order lemma bundle (Lemma 9.3h, Rmk 9.3h·A, Rmk 9.3i), and the Farey/factorial and two-gradings companions (Rmk II.5d, Rmk II.5e); and **v3.2.5** adds four kernel items — **Thm II.3c** (Superclass Hasse–Harmonic Bridge, seat II.3 after Rmk II.3b; item locked 2026-07-14), **Rmk 9.3j** (Log-mirror phase rigidity, seat §9.3 after Rmk 9.3i; item locked 2026-07-06), **Rmk II.5f** (Staircase Ford chains, seat II.5 after Rmk II.5e; item locked 2026-07-14 v1.0), and **Lemma 9.2a** (Finite-Ideal Frontier Law for the Stern–Brocot Tree, seat Part II / II.13 after §9.2; kernel routing **locked by Robin 2026-07-14** via the ratified amendment correcting the WO-SB/M kernel-non-contact clause; statement/proofs **cold-passed by Codex 2026-07-14** (PASS-WITH-PATCHES, both applied); **lemma LOCKED by Robin 2026-07-14**) — with two bibliography-tier splices (Architecture Note **[ANL-3]** Two-Continuum Effective-Tameness Boundary, locked 2026-07-10; work-order pointer **[WO-SB/M]** Stern–Brocot viewers + Markov decoration, locked 2026-07-12, with the frontier law reseated out of it to Lemma 9.2a per Chris's amendment) — all additive, without modifying baseline theorem content.

declared_base_replacements.base_text: **Declared-shell restriction (§5.3, v3.2.0 scoped).** Signals of length or modulus $N$ are decomposed against divisor labels $q \mid N$. In the local $N_0 = 720$ worked shell, $H_{\mathrm{harm}}(720)$ has $720$ dimensions and its conductor labels are the $30$ divisors of $720$; the Hasse atom $\mathrm{Div}(720)$ has $30$ nodes. Operations that exceed the declared shell (e.g., reading channels indexed by primes not in $\pi(N)$) require lens expansion (Part IV / IV.1).

declared_base_replacements.base_text: **Roots-of-unity register discipline (v3.1.18).** Phase claims in the helix family, the atlas, and the §9.7 embedding are stated first in roots-of-unity form; degrees and decimals are display annotations only — labels for human sight, not the object. A "30° rotation" is, in kernel language, multiplication by $\zeta_{12}$; a visual zero is an algebraic cancellation among roots of unity (e.g. $1 + \omega_6^3 = 0$). For the $\Omega = 2$ slice of a constant six-prime crystal, the outer hexagon and inner star are the two $\mu_6$-cosets of $\mu_{12}$ — $\langle\omega_6\rangle$ (outer, even $\zeta_{12}$ powers) and $\zeta_{12}\langle\omega_6\rangle$ (inner star, odd powers) — and the inner star's two triangles are the $\mu_3$-cosets $\zeta_{12}\langle\zeta_3\rangle$ and $i\langle\zeta_3\rangle = \zeta_{12}^{3}\langle\zeta_3\rangle$. Metric magnitudes such as $\sqrt{3}/3$ are *not* roots of unity; they live in the conductor-enlarged real subfield under the $\sqrt{\cdot}$ clause of Lemma 9.7q (Part II / II.15). This is a representation discipline, not a theorem: no kernel claim is expanded. *Degrees are labels for human sight; roots of unity are the object.*
